solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Bag some bargains at Chelsea (7)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters of the following words are taken

annotation.surface: A shopper picks up a few bargains in a smart London district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bag' reads as the verb 'grab' in the surface, but it is the noun definition. Chelsea is a wealthy area of London.
annotation.definitionFit: A satchel is a bag carried on a shoulder strap.

entries.clue: Director’s cut extremely savage about End of Days (8)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take only the extreme letters of 'savage'
indicatorNotes.about: the first pieces go around the next one

blocks.note: to score is to cut a line into
first and last letters of SavagE
last letter of dayS, placed inside SCORE+SE

annotation.surface: A film director's cut is butchered by a brutal edit around the movie End of Days.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Director's cut' is a film phrase, but the 's is 'is' linking the definition to the wordplay. SCORESE takes S inside, after SCOR.
annotation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the American film director of Goodfellas and Taxi Driver.

entries.clue: Dicky mentoring father in recovery period (3,7,5)

indicatorNotes.Dicky: dicky means unsound or faulty, so the letters are in bad order

annotation.surface: A father who coaches someone while unwell, perhaps recovering from illness.
annotation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for unwell or unreliable, as in 'a dicky heart'.
annotation.definitionFit: The morning after a night of drinking is the time spent recovering from the hangover.

entries.clue: Do her autopsy drunk (5,5)

indicatorNotes.drunk: a drunk staggers about, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: An instruction to a tipsy pathologist to carry out a post-mortem.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb of an order, but it is the noun: a party, as in 'a birthday do'.
annotation.definitionFit: A do is a party, and a house party is one held at somebody's home.

entries.clue: Boisterous Liberal ate food without first husband (7)

indicatorNotes.without first: remove the first of the H's, the one at the front

blocks.note: ate food = HAD DISH; drop the first H (husband)

annotation.surface: A rowdy Liberal politician eats without their spouse.
annotation.walkthrough: Ate food expands to HAD DISH, and H for husband is a standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: Laddish behaviour is loud and rowdy, like a group of young men out drinking.

entries.clue: Start to pray, for example, like American stars (7)

annotation.definitionNote: plural definition for a single constellation, which is a group of stars

indicatorNotes.Start to: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only P is taken from 'pray'

annotation.surface: Someone begins to pray, much as Americans pray to their stars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American stars' suggests Hollywood or the flag, but 'stars' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Pegasus is a constellation in the northern sky, named after the winged horse.

entries.clue: Sign left on shelter with time-sharing? (7)

indicatorNotes.with time-sharing: the two words share one T (time), so it is written only once

blocks.note: port = the left side of a ship
TENT, whose T is shared with the end of PORT

annotation.surface: A notice pinned to a shelter, perhaps about a timeshare holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time-sharing' suggests holiday flats; here T is the abbreviation for time, and PORT and TENT overlap on it.
annotation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign or omen of something to come.

entries.clue: Clothes to boast about (4)

indicatorNotes.about: about as in 'about turn': the word faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: to brag is to boast; turned round

annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clothes worth boasting about, but 'about' is the instruction and 'to' is only a joint.
annotation.surface: Fine clothes worth showing off.
annotation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, especially of a distinctive kind.

entries.clue: Spontaneous outpouring when their warning is received (4-2-3-6)

indicatorNotes.is received: the outpouring takes in the other words

blocks.note: a spurt is a sudden gush
an omen is a warning; OFTHEM + OMEN go inside SPURT

annotation.surface: Emotion spills out the moment people hear a warning.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to read 'their warning' as one idea; the trick is to expand the pronoun into two words, 'of them'.
annotation.definitionFit: A spur-of-the-moment act is done on impulse, without planning.

entries.clue: Small snake is less happy (6)

blocks.note: the adder is Britain's venomous snake

annotation.surface: A small snake feels a little down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' only links the wordplay to the definition, which is the comparative 'less happy'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain comparative synonym: sad is unhappy, so sadder is less happy.

entries.clue: An impressionist painter not using frame (3)

indicatorNotes.not using frame: drop the outside letters, the frame round the word

blocks.note: MONET without its outer M and T

annotation.surface: An Impressionist painting shown unframed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'An impressionist painter' reads as one phrase, but 'An' alone is the definition. The frame fits the painting picture neatly.
annotation.definitionFit: 'An' and 'one' are interchangeable in 'an apple', 'one apple'.

entries.clue: Tube not fine enough? (11)

blocks.note: the Tube is the nickname of London's metro railway
split the answer into a prefix meaning 'insufficiently' plus the past tense of grind

annotation.surface: A tube whose contents, like coffee or flour, have not been ground finely enough.
annotation.walkthrough: The second meaning is whimsical, hence the question mark: coffee that is under-ground has not been ground enough.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tube is the familiar name for the London Underground.

entries.clue: Taking unusual role, stands out and coasts? (10)

indicatorNotes.Taking: the second word takes the first inside it
indicatorNotes.unusual: an unusual arrangement is not the normal one, so the letters of 'role' are put out of their usual order

blocks.note: to shine is to stand out

annotation.surface: An actor takes an odd part, excels, and then rests on their laurels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coasts' reads as a verb, doing little, but it is the plural noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Shorelines are coasts, where land meets sea.

entries.clue: House the French in slum (4)

annotation.surface: Accommodating French people in a run-down district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House' looks like a verb meaning accommodate, but it is the noun abbreviated.
annotation.definitionFit: A hole is a dingy, squalid place to live.

entries.clue: Sailor’s map of earth perhaps containing fish (5,5)

indicatorNotes.perhaps: earth is one example of a planet
indicatorNotes.containing: the first word holds the second

blocks.note: char is a fish of the trout family, placed inside PLANET

annotation.surface: A sailor's map of the world marking where the fish are.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Map of earth' runs the definition into the wordplay; 'of' splits them.
annotation.definitionFit: A plane chart is a nautical chart drawn on a flat projection.

entries.clue: Queen’s backed winner at racetrack (5)

indicatorNotes.backed: backed as in 'backed up': moved in reverse, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: The Queen has bet on a winning horse at the races.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backed' and 'racetrack' point to horse betting, but the winner is a racing driver.
annotation.definitionFit: Ayrton Senna was a three-time Formula One world champion.

entries.clue: One’s hobby? Intense competition (8)

blocks.note: hot = intense, as in hot pursuit
a plate is a race for a prize, as in a selling plate

annotation.surface: Someone's pastime is fiercely competitive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hobby' is read as 'hob-by', like a hob: a hotplate is a hob, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A hotplate is a hob, so a whimsical 'hobby' thing.

entries.clue: Maestro Pele turned up grasping move instantaneously (8)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, read from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.grasping: the words hold the answer within them

annotation.surface: The football maestro Pele flips upside down while keeping hold of the ball.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned' seems to be the reversal indicator, but it only lends its T; 'up' does the reversing.
annotation.definitionFit: To teleport is to move from place to place instantly.

entries.clue: Admit I had meal at that restaurant? (8)

annotation.surface: A diner owns up to having eaten at a particular restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'at that restaurant' gives IN IT, with 'restaurant' only there for the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: To initiate someone into a club is to admit them as a member.

entries.clue: I’m dizzy blonde, removing top on summit (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer speaks: 'I'm dizzy' stands for a dizzy person, a noun

indicatorNotes.removing top: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, so that letter comes off

blocks.note: the head of a valley or pass is its summit

annotation.surface: A self-deprecating blonde admits to being scatterbrained.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dizzy blonde' looks like one unit, but 'blonde' is FAIR in the wordplay. In a down clue, A on B puts A above B.
annotation.definitionFit: An airhead is a silly, empty-headed person, so a dizzy one.

entries.clue: Repeat from memory entertaining new lies about temptress? (7)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: the first word takes in the letter
indicatorNotes.lies about: the whole lies turned about, reversed

blocks.note: to recite is to repeat from memory
N = new, placed inside RECITE; then turned round

annotation.surface: A witness keeps repeating rehearsed lies about a seductive woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lies' looks like falsehoods, but here it means 'rests'. The question mark marks temptress as one kind of enticer.
annotation.definitionFit: A temptress is a woman who entices, so an example of an enticer.

entries.clue: Relative back at home retches periodically (5)

indicatorNotes.periodically: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so only every second letter is used

annotation.surface: A relative back home is being sick now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back' belongs to 'at home' only; 'retches' is not reversed, its even letters are read forwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a niece, a sibling's daughter, is one kind of relative.

entries.clue: Highlight clue for Eid (4,2)

blocks.note: FLAG = DIE; DIE up (reversed in a down clue) = EID

indicatorNotes.clue for: the answer is itself a clue whose solution is the next word

annotation.surface: Pointing out a hint about the Muslim festival.
annotation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as a clue, leads to Eid. To flag is to weaken, or die, and 'up' reverses DIE.
annotation.definitionFit: To flag something up is to draw attention to it.

entries.clue: Escort begs to take clothes off (4)

indicatorNotes.to take clothes off: strip the outer letters, the clothing round the word

blocks.note: PLEADS (begs) without its outer P and S

annotation.surface: An escort pleads with someone to undress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Escort' looks like a noun, but it is the verb, as in 'escort someone to their seat'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: you lead a guest to the table when you escort them there.

entries.clue: Notice czar relocated in far north (6,4)

indicatorNotes.relocated: the letters are moved to new places

annotation.surface: An announcement that a Russian tsar has been exiled to Siberia.
annotation.walkthrough: A czar (tsar) was a Russian emperor, which suits a surface about banishment to the frozen north.
annotation.definitionFit: The Arctic zone is the region around the North Pole.

entries.clue: Prohibit class A drug, the cause of much distress (4)

blocks.note: E = ecstasy, a class A drug in UK law

annotation.surface: A call to outlaw a hard drug that causes much misery.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the long tail of the clue; 'class A' is the top UK drug category, which includes ecstasy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bane originally meant a poison, and now means whatever ruins or plagues you.

entries.clue: Spill tea on Dieter’s good waterproof material (5-6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B

blocks.note: gut is German for good; Dieter is a typical German name
a spill is a thin strip for lighting a fire, a taper

annotation.surface: Someone knocks tea over a dieter's fabric, luckily waterproof.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spill' looks like the verb, but it is the noun: a taper. 'Dieter' is not a slimmer but a German man.
annotation.definitionFit: Gutta-percha is a rubbery latex once used to waterproof cables and golf balls.

entries.clue: I try to follow Earl (3)

indicatorNotes.to follow: the second part comes after the first

annotation.surface: Someone aims to be a follower of an earl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I' at the front looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for I, and means the self.

entries.clue: Essentially, setter had heavenly body (7)

blocks.note: the setter is 'I', so setter had = I'd

annotation.surface: At heart, the crossword compiler had a heavenly figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' suggests a beautiful figure, but it is a meteor.
annotation.definitionFit: A Perseid is a meteor from the shower that peaks every August.

entries.clue: Knock airport evacuated repeatedly after introduction of robots (3-1-3)

indicatorNotes.introduction of: an introduction comes at the beginning, so only the opening letter of 'robots' is used
indicatorNotes.evacuated: emptied of its inside, leaving the outer letters

annotation.surface: An airport is cleared again and again after robots arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' leaves the count open; the enumeration shows AT appears three times.
annotation.definitionFit: Rat-a-tat is the sound of a sharp repeated knock on a door.
